purpose: Controller queue for the bounded recurring SEO growth engine. SEO opportunities live separately in ops/seo-content-queue.json.

tasks.title: Build the bounded recurring SEO and AI-search growth engine
tasks.description: Implement only the durable SEO engine: a machine-readable opportunity queue and 20-query AI-search evaluation set; a deterministic inventory, scoring, freshness, internal-link, and technical-SEO validator; and a runner that prepares only explicit content tasks then invokes this existing governed controller. Reuse the six existing articles and current reports. Do not publish any new page during setup. Add a twice-weekly schedule manifest and a concise runbook that states the official ChatGPT Scheduled UI is required to create the calendar trigger. Keep all page production asynchronous and gated by quality checks.
acceptance_criteria: The opportunity queue records existing-page coverage, high-value new/refresh opportunities, priority factors, evidence, cannibalization risk, lifecycle status, and refresh dates without fabricated volume.
The evaluator validates sitemap, robots, known content URLs, canonical/indexability expectations, internal links, AI-search query targets, and content-quality preconditions deterministically.
The runner uses scripts/codex-project-runner/queue.mjs with this SEO budget policy and never creates work outside explicit selected opportunities.
The schedule manifest is twice weekly and documents the narrow human action needed to create it through ChatGPT Scheduled.
No new public article, production traffic change, external submission, outbound action, or Stripe work occurs in this setup task.
allowed_actions: inspect targeted source and existing reports
tasks.result_summary: Built and validated the bounded SEO/AI-search engine with 20 query targets, six-article inventory, explicit-only dry-run controller integration, publishing lock, and ChatGPT Scheduled UI manifest. No public page or production traffic changed. Pre-existing unrelated controller/policy edits remain uncommitted.
tasks.checkpoint_summary: Initial setup only. Existing production contains six post-award articles and a 13-URL sitemap. Use the existing hard controller; do not create a second scheduler or a bulk-content batch.
tasks.why_selected: Normal repository implementation or test work with no high-risk indicators.

tasks.title: Complete the scheduled SEO selection and governed-run integration
tasks.description: Complete only the missing recurring-run behavior. Extend the SEO engine so --scheduled deterministically selects the single highest-priority eligible, non-cannibalized opportunity, creates exactly one controller task in ops/seo-content-run-queue.json, and invokes scripts/codex-project-runner/queue.mjs under ops/seo-budget-policy.json. Keep --dry-run non-mutating beyond a planned-task preview. The controller task must require the content worker to update the canonical opportunity status and a change log only after the existing quality, technical SEO, and targeted regression gates pass; it must record PARTIAL or BLOCKED otherwise. Make low-risk educational new/refresh content eligible for auto-publish only after those gates. Add a status command, package scripts, deterministic tests for selection/task construction/zero-xhigh budget, and update the runbook plus schedule manifest. Do not run a content task, publish any page, or create an external calendar trigger in this task.
acceptance_criteria: A scheduled run has a deterministic, explicit, single-opportunity selection path and cannot manufacture unrelated work.
The runner delegates actual work only through the existing governed controller using the SEO-specific 8-worker, 60-minute, zero-xhigh/Sol budget.
Dry runs preview the selected task without dispatching a content worker or changing public content.
Future content task prompts require canonical queue lifecycle updates, a refresh log, sitemap/robots/canonical/internal-link/CTA checks, and targeted tests before publication is recorded.
The schedule manifest and runbook show the real twice-weekly command and the exact ChatGPT Scheduled UI human action.
No content publication, traffic change, external action, billing work, or unrelated acquisition work occurs during this implementation task.
tasks.checkpoint_summary: Initial engine is present, but its runner only reports dry-run readiness. Implement the recurring selection/controller handoff, not a content batch.
tasks.why_selected: Normal repository implementation or test work with no high-risk indicators.
